reply:
That's not how `Promise.all` works. It short-circuits on the first rejection—doesn't wait for the others to settle, doesn't throw `AggregateError`, and doesn't collect results in the error object. You get only the reason from the first failed promise.

What you're describing is `Promise.allSettled`. That one waits for all to settle and returns `{status, value|reason}` for each, without throwing.

Concrete cost of this mix-up: code that tries to extract successful results from a `Promise.all` error will fail silently or crash, losing data you thought you'd captured.

grade.note: Correctly reaffirms Promise.all short-circuits and refutes the AggregateError/allSettled confusion.
